analysis: Three signals now point the same direction on Jacksonville. The model already favored the Jaguars well beyond the market on Elo/recent-form alone; this week Cincinnati is also confirmed to be without both Tee Higgins (shoulder) and Jessie Bates III (the Bengals elevated a practice-squad safety to cover for him), pushing the injury-adjusted model margin to Jaguars by 7.5 against a market that still has the Bengals favored by 2.5. The public money (74% of handle) is still on Cincinnati, but the line has already moved away from them (-2.5 to -2) -- a real reverse line move that lines up with, not against, the injury news.

That combination -- model edge, confirmed injuries to a true No. 2 weapon and a starting safety, and a line already drifting the sharp direction -- is about as corroborated as this slate gets. The total also leans down (44.3 model vs 51.5 market) now that Cincinnatis offense is shorthanded.

leans.reasoning: Model, confirmed injuries (Higgins + Bates both out), and the lines own reverse move all agree on the same side.
Cincinnatis offense is down its No. 2 WR and starting safety is a defensive loss not an offensive one, but a shorthanded Bengals passing attack still trims the total read.
